question: As Golden Lattice moves toward daily-driver use, do the three peers get tool access (web search, code execution, file read, MCP) during the protocol, and if so in what shape? Tool results are asymmetrically-introduced information that directly threatens invariant 2 (symmetric visibility: all peers see the same prompt/peer-outputs/dialogue-state); the choice of what to investigate threatens invariant 1 (no authority gradient) if any single model decides. Shapes to evaluate, none chosen: (a) shared-evidence-surface — tools called, results made symmetrically visible to all peers before they reason; preserves invariant 2 but raises a who-chooses-the-investigation authority-gradient subtlety. (b) independent per-peer investigation in Phase 1 — preserves independence, breaks symmetric visibility, requires Phase 2 cross-reading to surface evidentiary asymmetry (not just framing asymmetry) and parity metrics to account for tool-grounded claims. (c) orthogonal regardless of shape: Claim schema may need tool-provenance and the irreducibility trace must cover tool-grounded claims. This is a CONTRIBUTING.md spec-amendment-discipline decision (must come from real need, be structurally enforceable, tested, chronicled), explicitly NOT a feature toggle — CONTRIBUTING names 'features that bypass the four invariants' as the prototypical anti-contribution. On the critical path to the daily-driver goal because a co-authorship engine that cannot investigate is weak as a daily driver. Anthony to steer the shape; unresolved.
